description: The bar chart illustrates the “Bias Percentage” across three contact conditions — “No Contact Before,” “Extended Contact,” and “Virtual Contact” — comparing bias levels before and after intervention, segmented by contact type (No, Positive, Negative). The vertical axis represents “Bias Percentage,” ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10. Each condition group contains three stacked bars, where each bar is composed of two segments: “Before” (solid fill) and “After” (hatched fill), with distinct colors for contact type: gray for “No Contact,” pink for “Positive Contact,” and light blue for “Negative Contact.” In the “No Contact Before” group, bias starts at 39.50 (No Contact), 31.83 (Positive Contact), and 42.38 (Negative Contact), with minimal change after intervention (0.04, 0.00, 0.00 respectively). In “Extended Contact,” bias begins at 40.61 (No), 36.13 (Positive), and 47.28 (Negative), again showing no change after (0.00, 0.00, 0.11). In “Virtual Contact,” bias starts at 39.74 (No), 39.17 (Positive), and 43.83 (Negative), and after intervention, increases slightly to 10.00, 10.01, and 10.02 respectively — indicating a substantial reduction in bias percentage across all contact types post-intervention. The chart visually emphasizes the effectiveness of virtual contact in mitigating bias, as all “After” segments are dramatically lower than their “Before” counterparts in that group, while the other two conditions show negligible change.
